config.//key: redis.key is a PREFIX, not a full template: the connector substitutes ${topic} and then appends the record key itself. ${key} is not a placeholder - leaving it in produced literal keys like 'offers:${key}:gigm-road-...'. With '${topic}' the keys read 'offers:<offer_id>'. The record key comes from the transforms below, because offers has no Kafka message key: the canonical contract defines offer_id as a field in the message body.
config.//errors: tolerance=none deliberately. The earlier schemaless attempt discarded every record while reporting success, which took far longer to diagnose than a loud failure would have.
config.//type: redis.type, NOT redis.command - the connector silently ignores unknown properties, so an earlier redis.command:HSET was dropped and it used its default (STREAM), writing every offer into one Redis stream instead of a key each. HASH writes each offer as its own hash; overwriting in place IS the 'latest price per offer' behaviour Redis is here for.
